subject: Edge platform renewal & short vendor fallback eval
messages:
From: Cloudflare Renewals <renewals@cloudflare.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com
Cc: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-25T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal: Cloudflare edge + WAF – options and timeline

Hi Olga,

Hope you’re well — our records show Redwood’s current account for Cloudflare (Account ID: 982-RED) comes up for renewal on 2026-12-14. I’ve attached a short options pack with recommended SKUs, performance tiers, and an estimated TCO if you retain the same throughput profile.

Attachments: Cloudflare_Renewal_Options_Q4.pdf (pdf)

Quick highlights:
- Standard plan + Bot Management add-on looks like the closest feature match to your current usage.
- We can offer a 7% platform credit for a 12-month renewal, or 2% for 24 months with committed throughput.
- We can provide a 60-day grace for signature if you need additional procurement time — please confirm in writing.

Would you like a pricing walk-through next week? Happy to include a solutions engineer to run the traffic-profile mapping.

Best,
Lena Morales
Renewals Manager, Cloudflare
renewals@cloudflare.com

Cloudflare_Renewal_Options_Q4.pdf (attached)

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-10-26T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: Cloudflare edge + WAF – options and timeline

Lena — thanks for the package. Quick request and some context from our side:

1) Please send an itemized SOW / SKU worksheet that ties exactly to the line-items in the PDF (token/inspect rates, WAF rule packs, bandwidth tiers). We need those to run through purchasing and cost-ops.
2) Can you confirm whether the 7% credit is applied to platform usage only or to add-ons as well?
3) We are evaluating a short resilience/fallback run against Fastly and Akamai to validate multi-vendor fallbacks. That process may change our final sizing (we may choose a smaller committed footprint and rely on overflow policies).
4) Given the timing, we’d like to request a 90-day extension on the effective renewal date while we complete the fallback check and procurement approvals. Please confirm in writing if that’s possible.

CC’ing our procurement and infra leads: Stephanie (procurement) will own the PO/contract redlines; Vivek will validate performance and feature parity; Marcus will engage with alternative vendors.

Action for Cloudflare: please send the SKU worksheet and an editable contract redline template.

Thanks,
Olga
Director, Infrastructure Procurement
Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Renewal: Cloudflare edge + WAF – internal plan & asks

Team — looping you in with Lena’s package (see original email). Short internal plan so we’re aligned before we respond to vendors: 

Objective: preserve production reliability while buying time to validate a multi-vendor fallback (CF → Fastly / Akamai) and squeeze better commercial terms.

Proposed split of work:
- Stephanie: Lead procurement negotiations with Cloudflare (request SKU worksheet, push for 90-day extension, ask for a one-time credit tied to overflow traffic). Also own legal redline path and PO timing.
- Vivek: Run a short perf/feature matrix against our baseline traffic (3 endpoints, spike test, 95th/99th P95 latency). Focus on WAF false-positive profile and bot mitigation efficacy. Use the staging tenant creds; I’ll forward the access.
- Marcus: Reach out to Fastly and Akamai contacts to get quick PO-level quotes and engineering availability for a short POC. Ask both for: 1) emergency fallback pricing, 2) runbook for prefix failover, 3) SLA on cache-warmup.

Timing:
- Week 1 (Oct 29–Nov 4): procurement gets price worksheets & vendor calls scheduled.
- Week 2 (Nov 5–Nov 11): infra runs perf checks; Marcus coordinates POC windows.
- Week 3 (Nov 12–Nov 18): consolidate results, present recommendation, and finalize either a 90-day short-term extension with Cloudflare or commit to a staged migration.

Please confirm you can take these actions. I’ll draft the reply to Cloudflare asking for the 90-day formal extension and the SKU worksheet unless you see a reason to ask for a longer extension.

Thanks — OLGA

Lena — short update and next steps from Redwood: thank you for the options pack. After a quick triage with our infra and procurement teams we have two asks before we proceed to a signed order: 

1) Please confirm a 90-day extension of the current pricing/terms while we complete a short, targeted fallback evaluation against Fastly and Akamai. A formal written acknowledgement will be sufficient.

2) Provide an itemized SKU worksheet and an editable redline of the contract (track changes preferred). If you can include estimated overage rates for bandwidth spikes, that will help our cost model.

We plan a vendor scoping call the week of Nov 15 — please share availability for a 30–45 minute call and include a solutions engineer and your legal/account rep.

Attached is our internal evaluation summary template we will use to compare options: edge-vendor-eval-summary.csv (csv)

If Cloudflare can confirm the extension and share the worksheets by Nov 12, we’ll schedule the scoping call and keep the process moving. Otherwise we’ll need to evaluate accelerated alternatives.

Best,
Olga Petrov
